checks: Read out/q30/co13.log. The 1.0" ratios in the log match the report: S peak 12.2/1.22 K = 10.0 and HCN-FWHM mean 12.4; N 12.7 and 14.7. These sit slightly below the summary's 10.8/13.3/13.6/15.2, which are said to be from the final circular-1.0" run (spec_1.0). The log shows a native-beam peak ratio of 10-11 at S. The ratio is robust at roughly 10-15 whichever way it is sampled, and the tau conclusion does not depend on the choice.

The convolution to a common beam is done channel by channel with a deconvolution kernel, and the 12CO and 13CO beams differ only slightly (0.82x0.68 vs 0.85x0.79). This is the standard matched-aperture approach. 13CO is detected at 18-70 sigma, so it is a real detection, not a marginal line. Agree.

The off-position ratio (11-17) is the same as at the cores. The 12/13 ratio is therefore nearly uniform across the region, and tau is a property of the whole CO medium, not of the cores. This supports the use of the ratio but means the cores are not special. The worker states it.

Tk bound: the arithmetic is the same as Q23 with tau replaced by the measured tau. S >=37 K (peak) / 26 K (HCN-mean) and N >=19 / 17 K at ff=1 are reproduced to within 1 K. Agree that tau is no longer the limiting assumption. R and ff are, and the report says so.

The conditional claim stands: tau>=3 holds only if R>~35-40. The report gives the R=25 case (tau 1.5-2.1) openly. This is acceptable. Only the lower-limit reading is claimed, not a measurement of tau.

fixes.what: Word the Q30b/Q30c statements as 'tau constrained given R', not as a measured Tk. In the result text, state that the bound is still a lower limit in two ways: (i) the 1.0" beam-averaged ratio is applied to the 0.26" component, and (ii) R is unconstrained.
fixes.why: The data fix 12CO/13CO. They do not fix tau without R. The 1.0" ratio is not the ratio of the 0.26" gas. The report already admits most of this, so only the headline wording needs care.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Quote tau as a function of R (done), and quote R priors from the literature: ~40-60 for LIRG disks, and larger (>~100) in the Arp 220-like nuclei, which would push tau to >=7. Carry that range to Tk. Say that R<~35 would require a nucleosynthetically unusual 13C-rich medium.

fixes.what: Add one sentence on C18O(2-1). The log shows the C18O velocity range was examined, but no C18O result is reported even though the question names it. Either give the 13CO/C18O ratio or an upper limit, or say that it is not covered or not detected, with a limit.
fixes.why: C18O is the standard cross-check on 13CO opacity and on R. Without it the 13CO-thin assumption (tau13 = tau12/R ~0.1) is not tested.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Measure 13CO/C18O in the same matched beam. A ratio near the isotope ratio (~3-8) means 13CO is thin. A ratio near 1 means 13CO is thick, so tau12 is larger than quoted and the bound gets stronger.

fixes.what: Remove or explain the native S 12CO noise of 0.015 mJy in co13.log (about 50x lower than the other cells).
fixes.why: It looks like a unit or sampling bug. The native S S/N is not used for the result, but it should not be left in an output file as is.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Measure the rms in the signal-free channels of the same cube and the same box, and check the pbcor against the flat-noise cube.

notes_for_questioner: Q30 is answered conditionally. tau(12CO 2-1) >= 3 holds for R >= ~40, and the Tk>=37 K (S) and >=19 K (N) bound at ff=1 stands, with ff as the open parameter. The thermalised CO(1-0)/(3-2)/(2-1) ratios at 2.5" probe only the cool beam-averaged gas, not the compact component. New questions: (1) Can R be tied to anything in the data, e.g. HCN/H13CN and HCO+/H13CO+ as an independent isotope-ratio check given team-b's H13CN(4-3) and Harada 1-0 lines? (2) The uniform 12/13 ratio (11-17) at cores and off-positions suggests the 13CO emission is cospatial with 12CO. Is a lower ff for the 0.26" T_b (the actual open parameter) constrained by the 0.26" vs 1.0" 12CO flux ratio, i.e. is the compact component resolved at 0.26"? That test needs no new data and would turn the ff=1 bound into a ff range.
